title: The Evolution of Agentic Harnesses: From Chains to Graph to Code
gist: LinkedIn Distinguished Engineer Karthik Ramgopal argues agentic harnesses have evolved from chains to graphs to code-execution loops, moving agents from best-effort to engineered reliability; he recommends choosing the least complex abstraction that meets reliability, speed and cost needs, and illustrates each stage with LinkedIn systems.

insights.claim: Agentic harnesses have progressed through three paradigms, Chains, Graphs and Code, marking a transition from ad hoc best-effort experiments to resilient production-grade architectures.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Gives investors and architects a maturity ladder for judging how robust an agent vendor's stack is.
insights.locator: Key Takeaways

insights.claim: Chains are linear prompt sequences that are fast to build and offer the lowest latency and compute cost, but they are fragile because a single upstream error cascades with no built-in way to detect or recover from it.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Cheap, narrow chain use cases remain economical but are not suited to high-stakes workflows.
insights.quote: A single mistake upstream would cascade through and derail the entire flow because there was no built-in mechanism to systematically detect or recover from the error.
insights.locator: While relatively fast to build and deploy

insights.claim: With chains, building the initial 80% of the experience was fast, but closing the final quality gap for production required extensive iteration through evaluations, prompt refinement and sustained engineering investment.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: The cost of AI products sits in the last 20%, so demo speed is a poor proxy for production cost.
insights.locator: This approach epitomized the "best-effort" nature

insights.claim: Graphs made control flow explicit and declarative via nodes and edges, enabling branching, parallelism, retries and state management, and mirroring the earlier evolution of data pipelines and distributed systems.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Agent engineering is repeating known distributed-systems patterns, so existing orchestration expertise transfers.
insights.locator: Graphs: Introducing Structure and Control

insights.claim: Graphs remain bounded automations around human-defined workflows, and as state spaces grow developers must encode ever more recovery and validation logic, producing brittle, hard-to-maintain flow definitions that are ill-suited to tasks not expressible as deterministic workflows.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Explains the push from workflow engines toward code-generating agents, with implications for workflow-builder products.
insights.locator: While graphs significantly expanded the complexity

insights.claim: Code harnesses treat code rather than prompts as the medium of reasoning: agents generate, execute and refine code in a sandbox, which replaces developer-defined workflows with solutions the agent finds through generated code with verifiable outputs.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Verification via execution gives agents a pass/fail signal that language output lacks, supporting autonomy in testable domains.
insights.locator: The most recent leap in agentic systems

insights.claim: Natural-language LLM output is probabilistic and inherently untrustworthy before validation, whereas code is deterministic: it either compiles, runs and gives the right output or fails, producing tight feedback loops that improve reliability.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Domains where output is testable are the best near-term candidates for autonomous agents.
insights.quote: A piece of code, however, is deterministic.
insights.locator: A natural language output from an LLM is probabilistic

insights.claim: A code-harness architecture relies on four components: an execution sandbox, instrumentation and logging, a validation harness of tests and assertions, and an iterative refinement loop that retries until correctness criteria are met.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: A checklist for evaluating whether an agent platform has real verification and not just prompting.
insights.locator: To ensure safety and correctness

insights.claim: An early LinkedIn generative AI agent used a fixed 3-step chain built with LangChain: routing, retrieval via tools such as Bing web search and internal LinkedIn APIs, and generation.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Even sophisticated incumbents began with simple chains and later outgrew them.
insights.locator: At LinkedIn, for example, one of our early Generative AI agents

insights.claim: LinkedIn built multi-agent orchestration by reusing its existing messaging system for long-lived tasks, gaining FIFO delivery, message history lookup, parallelism via threads, resilience through persistent retries and flexible sync or async streaming.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Reusing mature messaging infrastructure for agent orchestration is a pragmatic edge for incumbents with existing platforms.
insights.locator: At LinkedIn, we implemented orchestration

insights.claim: LinkedIn's graph workflow on LangGraph used conditional execution, retries and fallbacks, structured state management and explicit validation such as schema checks, business rules or secondary models, and it enabled Hiring Assistant, its first AI agent for recruiters.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Shows a production agent product built on graph harnesses, with validation as the main reliability tool.
insights.locator: The graph-based workflow was implemented atop LangGraph

insights.claim: Multi-agent graph systems needed first-class asynchronous agent-to-agent protocols like A2A and ACP, which eventually merged into A2A, and human-in-the-loop support was essential because agents were not fully autonomous.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Protocol consolidation around A2A reduces interoperability fragmentation among agents.
insights.locator: For many complex tasks, a single monolithic agent

insights.claim: LinkedIn modeled Cognitive Memory as another agent that application agents integrate with, because great agent experiences need domain intelligence, organizational context and memory to learn from interactions.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Memory as a separable service points to a distinct layer in the agent stack.
insights.locator: These agents also required advanced memory

insights.claim: LinkedIn's code-based analytics agent turns natural language questions into SQL and Python, runs them on sample data, validates against privacy, visibility and governance constraints, and iterates until correct, giving faster time-to-market and a more auditable, reproducible system than bespoke prompts, tools and workflow graphs.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Skipping bespoke workflow graphs cut build effort, a case for code harnesses in governed data analysis.
insights.locator: The agent translates the user query

insights.claim: Robust agentic systems at any stage should treat LLM outputs as untrusted input validated via schema checks, business and compliance rules or secondary models before influencing downstream logic.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Validation layers are table stakes and a differentiator in enterprise agent procurement.
insights.locator: Treat LLM Outputs as Untrusted Input

insights.claim: Planning should be decoupled from execution: the model proposes a plan but a strictly controlled software framework executes it, improving transparency and control.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Separation lets teams apply policy and approvals at the execution boundary.
insights.locator: Decouple Planning from Execution

insights.claim: Observability must capture state at each step, execution traces and validation results while masking sensitive information, since highly non-deterministic systems cannot be debugged without visibility.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Observability tooling for agents is a growing spend category.
insights.quote: You cannot debug a complex and highly non-deterministic system if you can't see what it's doing.
insights.locator: Invest in Observability

insights.claim: Agentic systems are iterative rather than static, so teams should build feedback loops that capture failures, evolve prompt, policy and procedural memory, and invest in evaluation and simulation environments.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Continuous evaluation infrastructure is an ongoing cost, not a launch task.
insights.locator: Build for Continuous Improvement

insights.claim: Use the least complex system that reliably solves the problem: chains suit narrow linear tasks like support drafts, summarization, moderation and extraction, and for many production workloads remain the most economically efficient option.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Simple architectures may capture most near-term enterprise value at the lowest cost.
insights.quote: Use the least complex system that reliably solves the problem.
insights.locator: Choosing the Right Abstraction

insights.claim: Graphs fit workflows needing branching, retries and state transitions, such as multi-step customer service, IT automation and compliance pipelines, but add orchestration latency and multiple LLM calls, so they are more reliable than chains but more expensive to design and operate.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Mid-complexity workflows trade cost for resilience.
insights.locator: Graphs become appropriate when workflows require

insights.claim: Coding harnesses suit software engineering, financial analysis, legal validation, scientific workflows and infrastructure automation where outputs can be tested or validated, and they incur the highest compute and latency costs but give the strongest guarantees when correctness outweighs speed or cost.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Highest-cost agent architectures concentrate in high-value verifiable domains, implying heavier inference demand there.
insights.locator: Coding harnesses are best suited for domains

insights.claim: Over-engineering is a common failure mode as models improve and costs fall, because sophisticated abstractions often raise compute spend, latency and operational complexity faster than business outcomes, so strong organizations win by optimizing capability per dollar rather than architectural sophistication.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Pushes back on adding agent complexity by default and favors cost-disciplined AI adopters.
insights.quote: Strong engineering organizations do not win by maximizing architectural sophistication; they win by optimizing capability per dollar.
insights.locator: The real advantage comes from disciplined abstraction selection

insights.claim: The developer role is shifting from Prompt Designer to System Architect, as success moves from crafting prompts to designing execution flows, managing state and dependencies, and building validation and recovery mechanisms.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Skills demand moves toward software architecture and reliability engineering, away from prompt craft.
insights.quote: We are witnessing a professional transition from the 'Prompt Designer' to the 'System Architect'.
insights.locator: The rapid evolution of agentic systems has triggered

insights.claim: Modern harnesses aim for determinism wherever possible, use controlled nondeterminism only where necessary and feature clear failure modes with defined recovery paths, so the novelty lies in integrating probabilistic models into deterministic frameworks rather than in the components.
insights.speaker: Karthik Ramgopal
insights.so_what: Value accrues to whoever builds the deterministic wrapper, not just the model.
insights.quote: The novelty is not in the components themselves, but in how they integrate probabilistic models into deterministic frameworks.
insights.locator: This progression marks the evolution of AI agents
